most_important.why: The only two high findings and both re-verified: the Linux release leg on floating ubuntu-latest ships AppImage/.deb artifacts with a glibc 2.38 floor that cannot start on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 or RHEL 9 while README promises 'most distributions'; and MSI/.deb installs are offered the NSIS/AppImage payload with no bundle_type() gate, so the enterprise MSI path is nagged every launch and one click installs a second conflicting copy. Both fixes are small (runner pin plus objdump guard; a pure updatable_format gate).

Three shared-state bugs with the same root: the docstrings' 'never run at once' premise is false given keep-alive views, so one Cancel button stops unrelated audits, bulk tenant writes, sweeps and probes, and the single throttle_observer slot lets concurrent fan-outs clobber each other's adaptive back-off. A run_id-based cancel and a multi-observer slot fix all three together.

The support log fails exactly when needed: an unwritable log dir panics the process before any subscriber or hook exists, webview panics never reach the backend log, and no Graph/ARM/KV request carries a client-request-id or captures request-id, so a 429 storm and a 5xx outage are indistinguishable and Microsoft support cannot correlate any non-Exchange failure.

F459 is the structural enabler behind the test-oracle slice: lifting bulk's private ProgressSink into progress.rs unblocks handler tests for audit, backup, restore, sharepoint and the tester. F450/F451/F448/F455 then name concrete missing regression tests that would have caught already-indexed bugs (F023, F037-F039, F022, F001/F004) by construction, several against seams that already exist.

End-to-end error UX: a 401 is a dead end whose hints tell the operator to sign out against the documented in-place re-auth design, the throttled message leaks Option Debug formatting, network errors drop their cause at all six sites, and non-Graph clients lack a connect timeout so firewalled hosts wait minutes for a cause-less error.

Launch cold path: three concurrent full /applications paginations that one $select superset covers (18 vs 6 round trips on 5k apps), multi-MB audit and inventory payloads shipped over IPC twice to render a few counts, and every restored dock pane firing its full detail fetch hidden before Home paints.

result.executive_summary: azapptoolkit is a mature, unusually well-documented codebase with an explicit safety contract (never under-report, never cache a degraded run, coverage is never overstated, a partial success is a real write) and a source-scanning invariants suite that pins many of those rules. Its strengths are real and consistent across slices: the pure decision cores (Exchange `verdict`/`targets`/`aap`, the LRU+TTL cache with its store-after-invalidate guard, the resource-aware scoping gates, the audit scorer) are fail-closed by construction and heavily table-tested; the Graph transport has one retrying core with verb-derived retry classes and same-origin guards; auth hardening (PKCE, state, nonce, tid/oid re-binding, chunked keyring, AADSTS redaction) is careful; IPC parity is exact at 186 commands; and the frontend has a single-writer open-items design, strong a11y foundations and a well-reasoned GUI harness. The dominant problem is results that mislead in the reassuring direction: a whole family of RBAC-scopable mailbox permissions scores as healthy, the 5000-site sweep and a swallowed SP lookup are cached as complete, backup Pass 3 thins silently, partial AAP migrations and vetoed one-click fixes toast success, and a restore that duplicates the estate is offered on screen as the re-run remedy. Second come documented controls that do nothing: the auto-update opt-out is never read, the install format is never checked, and the Linux artifact cannot start on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 or RHEL 9. Third are session and auth edges: a domain-form tenant id the config screen accepts can never sign in, `interaction_required` purges the whole session, sign-out fails open on a keyring error, and CAE-ness is missing from the token cache key. Fourth are engineering-debt clusters: three cancel flags shared across run kinds that the keep-alive UI lets overlap, frontend primitives bypassed at dozens of sites, invariant rules that pass vacuously, the Exchange transport outside the shared retry class and error taxonomy, and an orchestration layer with almost no handler-level tests. Finally, several load-bearing sentences in AGENTS.md and `docs/architecture/` now instruct contributors to do the wrong thing. Almost every fix has a precedent in the same file or a sibling module, and roughly half of the top items are small. Verification was strict: 131 claims were narrowed with a recorded correction and one was refuted. Start with the mailbox scoping tables and the dropped coverage signals (F151, F178, F023, F039), then the updater gate and the Linux runner pin, then the shared cancel flags.

top_priorities.title: Tenant-wide mailbox permissions invisible to the audit, and the EWS scope never gets a verdict
top_priorities.effort: S for the tables, M for the resolver
top_priorities.why: Both judges ranked this. mailbox_named at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:195 covers only Mail., MailboxSettings., Calendars. and Contacts., so an app holding Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All or MailboxItem.ImportExport.All gets a healthy row, no Scope fix and no high-risk points; this is the exact class the audit exists to catch. resolve_mail_scopes at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/mail_scopes.rs:108 hardcodes the Microsoft Graph resource, so EWS full_access_as_app shows Unknown forever and a correctly RBAC-scoped EWS app still scores org-wide. Start by extending mailbox_named with the MailboxItem./MailboxFolder./MailboxConfigItem./Mail-Advanced. prefixes plus HIGH_RISK_APP_PERMISSIONS entries at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/audit/permissions.rs:67 with a table test citing Microsoft's RBAC-for-Applications roles; then make the resolver accept (resource, value) pairs and add the joined resolver test F456 names at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/tests.rs:200.

top_priorities.title: Capped and degraded reads drop their signal and are cached as complete
top_priorities.why: Both judges ranked this. list_all_sites at crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:105 truncates at 5000 sites and returns no flag, so is_complete() is true, the per-app panel says the app reaches no site, and the result is cached for 60 minutes; score_one at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/audit.rs:1489 swallows a failed SP lookup and the run caches as a clean scan; permissions_resolve.rs:277 caches a degraded detail that shows granted permissions as not granted; backup Pass 3 at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/backup.rs:675 has no session latch and records nothing in skipped. The fix shape exists in each file: return (rows, truncated) as collect_all_pages_capped does and fold it into is_complete() (serde-defaulted truncated on the DTO at crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sharepoint.rs:130), return Err instead of None so the Transient classification marks the run degraded, skip the cache put on a degraded resolution, and thread SessionDead plus note_graph_failures into Pass 3 as Passes 1 and 2 already do.

top_priorities.title: The documented update opt-out is inert, MSI and .deb installs get the wrong payload, and Linux builds cannot start on current LTS distros
top_priorities.why: Both judges ranked this. UserSettings::load, the only reader of AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE, has no production caller, so every launch egresses to GitHub against the README's MDM promise; check_for_update at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26 never consults tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type(), so an MSI operator who clicks Update gets a second per-user NSIS install and a .deb install downloads the AppImage and fails with a raw plugin string. The Linux release leg at .github/workflows/release.yml:105 runs on floating ubuntu-latest, so the AppImage and .deb import GLIBC_2.38 and fail at exec on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and RHEL 9. Add a pure update_policy(auto_update, bundle_type) function with a unit test, make the DTO tri-state so shell.rs can hide or relabel the menu item, pin the Linux runner to ubuntu-22.04 and add an objdump -T guard step that fails when the max GLIBC_ version exceeds 2.35.

top_priorities.title: One Cancel button stops every long run of every kind, and concurrent fan-outs clobber each other's throttle
top_priorities.why: Both judges ranked this. audit_cancel is claimed by the read-only audit, all 11 bulk_* writes and the AAP migration; sweep_cancel by the site, Key Vault and mailbox sweeps; dr_cancel by backup and restore. Every top-level view is keep-alive and CancelFlag::cancel stamps every older generation, so the docstring at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/bulk.rs:127 (never run at once) is a false premise and cancelling a scan can halt a bulk delete mid-selection. GraphClient has a single throttle_observer slot (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/throttle.rs:141), so whichever run drops first clears the survivor's adaptive back-off. Add bulk_cancel and migration_cancel to AppState, split sweep_cancel at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/permission_tester.rs:443, pin command-to-flag in repo_invariants/cancel.rs, and make clear_throttle_observer compare-and-clear; every frontend Cancel handler must then call its own command.

top_priorities.title: The Exchange transport sits outside the shared retry class and error taxonomy, and the invariant that should catch it passes vacuously
top_priorities.why: Both judges ranked this. send_core at crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client/transport.rs:265 open-codes its retry loop, so a New-ManagementRoleAssignment that committed before a 502 is replayed, fails as a duplicate and grants.rs then keeps the org-wide grant with 'scoping is NOT effective'; repo_invariants/trust.rs:163 skips any file without with_retries(. The verifier refuted the earlier duplicate-assignment headline, so the accurate framing is false failures. Two siblings ride along: rbac.rs:220 lists references through invoke_optional so a misclassified 400 can unlock an irreversible group delete, and targets.rs:716 compares DNs case-sensitively while the post-write proof folds case. Port send_core onto with_retries with a retry_class_for(cmdlet) helper, make the trust rule fail any crate referencing MAX_RETRIES or next_backoff_ms directly, and add an Exchange error_conformance.rs mirroring ARM's.

top_priorities.title: Restore is not idempotent while the DR view and the restore report both tell the operator to re-run it
top_priorities.why: Operator-risk lens. In the one scenario DR exists for, following the on-screen remedy at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dr.rs:502 ('recreates only what is missing') creates a second copy of every already-restored app with new appIds, paired SPs, fresh 180-day secrets and re-granted admin consent, and the Restore button stays live after a successful run. restore.rs:751 repeats the re-run instruction and restore.rs:734 reports failed Graph reads as runbook facts. Reword the callout and clear the loaded plan after report.set, stop the report saying re-run the restore, then make Pass 1 (restore.rs:197) adoption-aware by display name plus a source marker.

top_priorities.title: Give the orchestration layer a test seam
top_priorities.why: Engineering-leverage lens. Roughly twenty confirmed bugs (F001, F004, F023, F037, F038, F039, F054, F070 to F075, F460) live in State- or AppHandle-bound bodies that no test can construct; only credentials.rs and backup.rs have wiremock handler tests, and bulk.rs proved the ProgressSink seam works then kept it private. Lift the trait from bulk.rs:46 into apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/progress.rs:21 as pub(crate) with a test Recorder, replace the closure at backup.rs:364, add commands/test_support.rs with one mock base-URL convention and shared builders, then write the three F455 tests against permissions.rs:618 and permissions.rs:389, which already take &GraphClient and need no refactor.

top_priorities.title: The SSO claims editor detaches a live policy from an empty editor and writes transformation claims that can never be emitted
top_priorities.why: Operator-risk lens. A first-time operator without Policy.ReadWrite consent has the claims read swallowed to None at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/mod.rs:510, the tab at sso_tab.rs:543 renders an empty editor, and one Save detaches the configured policy; each save also orphans a tenant-level claimsMappingPolicy because set_claims_mapping (mod.rs:1643) unassigns and recreates instead of PATCHing. The codec at sso/claims.rs:48 emits TransformationID instead of ID and conflates both on read, and the round-trip test at claims.rs:442 pins the wrong shape. Add a claims_read_failed discriminator to SsoConfigDto, disable Save until a successful read with a Load-claims consent button, add transformation_id to the schema entry DTO, and replace the masking test with Microsoft's documented fixture.

top_priorities.title: Pin the IPC contract mechanically and stop a non-UiError rejection from aborting the WASM app
top_priorities.why: Engineering-leverage lens. Command, arg-struct and return-type parity is exact today (186 = 186 = 186) but is checked only by .claude/hooks/command-parity-check.sh:15, an advisory hook that always exits 0 and needs jq; invoke_result at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/bindings/mod.rs:17 unwraps the error deserialization, so any string rejection (invalid args, ACL) panics the whole frontend. Add repo_invariants/ipc.rs reusing sources::commands() with a vacuity floor, wrap invoke_result to deserialize through serde_json::Value and map a non-UiError rejection to UiError::new("ipc", ..), and move DirectoryIndexStatus (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/applications/mod.rs:86) into the DTO crate.

top_priorities.title: Audit-surface fixes report success while doing nothing or dropping warnings
top_priorities.why: Operator-risk lens. The Permissions-tab AAP migration gate at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/exchange_scoping_section.rs:324 checks only failures, so a partial report (legacy policy kept, fail-closed) toasts Migrated while the sibling audit dialog gates correctly; the redundant-permissions Fix at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/remediation.rs:257 returns empty removed and skipped when every value is vetoed and the UI hides the button; scope_remediation.rs:111 hard-codes zero warnings so 'groups were NOT applied' reads as clean; permissions_tab.rs:116 sets its outcome note right before on_changed unmounts it. Add AapMigrationReport::is_clean() on the DTO (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/exchange.rs:174) and use it on both surfaces, push vetoed values into skipped, gate on_done on a non-empty removed, read res.warnings.len(), and toast failures before on_changed.

top_priorities.title: Error codes are produced consistently but consumed inconsistently
top_priorities.why: Engineering-leverage lens. consent_required is flattened to token_error inside every client call (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:129), so the shared consent fallback never fires for scoped calls; the throttled message at http_error.rs:76 reads 'retry after Some(30)s'; .toast__message at apps/desktop/web-rs/styles.css:3513 collapses the appended hint; only Graph has a connect timeout, so ARM, Key Vault and Exchange spin about four minutes against a firewalled host (crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/client.rs:38); the inline-error path at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/hooks/use_command.rs:85 (24 call sites) never offers Re-authenticate; and a 401 renders as bare text with hints that say sign out against the in-place re-auth design. Each is a one-file change on a shared producer or sink and reaches every surface at once.

top_priorities.title: The permission tester reports a definitive no_access when its reads failed, and never sees EWS-only holders
top_priorities.why: Operator-risk lens. orgwide_mailbox_grant at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/permission_tester.rs:63 folds a failed Graph read into EntraReach::NotHeld; test_site_access at :1092 prints 'holds no organization-wide SharePoint grant' when the grants read failed; find_mailbox_reachers at :466 discovers candidates from the Graph resource only, so a principal with full_access_as_app over every mailbox is reported as no_access. An admin uses these answers to decide who can read a mailbox. Return a tri-state (Held / None / Unreadable), score Unreadable as unknown in synthesize, page appRoleAssignedTo on both mailbox resources, and let exchange_available reflect the real degraded mode so the documented partial-coverage caveat can fire.
